# Numeric row cut: source and proof map

Read-only analysis, 2026-10-13. No runtime or diagnostic code was changed. Line references below refer to the isolated archived source in `../snapshot/`, which has batch-boundary diagnostic marks; the only live product delta observed is the adjacent-token lookup cache in `src/vdom_snapshot_runtime.ts:3312-3328`. The archived executor performs a map lookup for every packed cell at `../snapshot/src/vdom_snapshot_runtime.ts:3325`. The live cache reuses the previous record for adjacent equal tokens. It is **unqualified** against the frozen build04 product baseline, and is not included in the diagnostic snapshot. The 128 and 1024 count recordings cited below are operation evidence only; they do not establish a removable time fraction or a physical implementation choice.

## Concrete ownership and creation chain

1. The archived OXC analysis accepts a numeric sink only when state reads are owner-local, immutable, numeric, absent from outside reads, and the expression passes its closed primitive syntax/purity checks (`../snapshot/compiler/oxc-spike/src/main.rs:3780-3890`, `:4085-4095`). Derived-local expansion and budget checks precede certification (`:390-500`). The emitted owner kernel rewrites each certified state reference to `rowState.inputValues[slot]`, dispatches by changed slot, tracks `seenMask`, compares output with `Object.is`-equivalent number behavior, and stages changed primitive outputs (`../snapshot/compiler/oxc-spike/src/owner_update_program.rs:89-199`). It does not call an authored projector in its emitted body.
2. OXC emits the kernel table and `defineComponent(..., {stateLayout, ownerUpdateProgram})` registration for an eligible component (`../snapshot/compiler/oxc-spike/src/main.rs:4097-4136`, `:4200-4258`). The frozen build04 proof contains `NativeRowA/B` program IDs, three sites and three sinks each. The diagnostic build lock checks these exact native assertion, registration and kernel identities against that proof; the asset bytes can differ because of probes.
3. `defineComponent` matches component, layout and program IDs, then normalizes and associates the program (`../snapshot/src/component_state_runtime.ts:272-326`). Normalization copies/freezes slot descriptors, checks contiguous unique slot numbers and caches by layout object (`../snapshot/src/compiled_state_layout.ts:62-134`); association checks schema, slot/sink bounds, unique sink IDs, callable `executeCut`, and rejects conflicting registrations (`:138-204`). World creates layout-backed lanes and row leases (`../snapshot/src/owner_state_world.ts:552-705`), then `numericRowForCell(handle,version)` validates committed identity, version, row identity, generation, lane, layout, source and lease (`:1745-1790`).
4. VDOM `prepareNumericRowProgram(view)` accepts only direct writes in an uncompiled graph, checks layout, slot/column correspondence, distinct sources, all binding descriptors and owner/source-site membership, then proves sink ID completeness and per-slot order before attaching a kernel (`../snapshot/src/vdom_snapshot_runtime.ts:2398-2617`). It keeps token and row identity indexes and invalidates them on source binding changes (`:2618-2638`, `:4020-4080`, `:4232-4278`, `:4330-4350`). Root caches row tokens by row identity and captures exact World handles/versions (`../snapshot/src/component_state_runtime.ts:4888-4930`); its arrays are `#` private, while VDOM's `executePreparedNumericRows` is a public method accepting caller arrays (`../snapshot/src/vdom_snapshot_runtime.ts:2643-2666`). The opaque branded token is a TypeScript type and a frozen object; it is not authority for trusting arbitrary array contents.

The compiler proof is **build/source provenance**, not an unforgeable runtime capability. `defineComponent` and `bindSources` are exported and accept structural metadata/functions (`../snapshot/src/component_state_runtime.ts:272-326`; `../snapshot/src/jsx_binding_runtime.ts:205-245`). `associateCompiledOwnerUpdateProgram` validates shape and IDs but not that `executeCut` is the compiler-emitted closed body (`../snapshot/src/compiled_state_layout.ts:138-199`). VDOM preparation verifies graph membership and sink layout, not function purity. An internal compiler-owned registry/brand could establish provenance under a conforming generated-caller contract, but a brand, type, or build hash alone does not prove that an arbitrary JavaScript function has no captured callbacks/globals or other effects. Certificate issuance and a proof method for closed execution are open design obligations. A specialization that skips staging/validation or treats a kernel as effect-free must resolve those obligations or retain the current checks. Merely seeing schema v2 or a function-valued field cannot distinguish an emitted kernel from user-supplied metadata.

## Existing passes and what may be retired

Let `C` be captured cells, `R` distinct affected rows, `S` layout slots per row, `D` reached dependency slots and `K` selected sinks. Counts are visits, not nanoseconds. In the measured all-dirty workload, `C=3R`, `S=3`, `K=3R`. `count-native-128` records 92,160 input cells, 30,720 distinct rows and 92,160 host writes over 240 measured frames; `count-native-1024` records 737,280, 245,760 and 737,280 respectively (records under `../runs/count-native-{128,1024}-*/record.json`). `native.setter.calls` is **one per row callback**, each callback invokes three actual state setters; it is not a count of individual setter invocations. Both records have `PASS`, but these counters alone do not select a mechanism.

| Pass / location | Authority and freshness | Possible replacement, required proof, retired old work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pending cut capture `pending_state_changes.ts:84-107`; Root `:5081-5106` | Queue membership and exact handle/version are mutable until capture; legacy entries can decline. Root arrays are private. | A direct per-row dirty journal could replace the capture loop only if it preserves coalescing, exact versioned acknowledgement and callback order. Recording: counted queue visits, allocation and fallback incidence, plus reentrant/legacy behavior proof. Retire the existing queue traversal only after the replacement owns those obligations; adding a second row queue is no reduction. |
| World resolution Root `:4888-4930`, World `:1745-1790` | Handle identity, cell version, promotion, row lease/generation and value are live. Root token map is a cache, not authority. | A World-issued cut lease could combine resolution with capture **if** lease revocation is proved across dispatch/updater callbacks, owner retirement, promotion and row reuse. Recording: `native.resolve` time and exact World lookup count. Retire the repeated `numericRowForCell` path, not merely cache its result beside it. |
| Packed VDOM validation `vdom_snapshot_runtime.ts:3275-3350` | Count/buffer bounds and token membership are API boundary checks; source/column lease, row capacity, duplicate value agreement and row epoch are live. Snapshot root, token and metadata are private records; inputs remain caller-provided. The live adjacent-token patch removes some Map.get calls only. | A Root-private executor or immutable cut descriptor might replace per-cell token-map lookup after proving no caller can reach it with unaudited buffers and that binding changes revoke the descriptor. Recording: separate map lookup/duplicate counts and a **future independently source/build-locked qualification** of the unqualified adjacent-token patch, followed by semantics cases for wrong indices/duplicate conflicts. Existing 128/1024 records are prepatch controls, not a patch comparison. Retire the lookup and repeated structural checks in that private path; keep public API preflight. |
| Dependency gather `:3350-3380` | `usedSlots` and sink topology are prepared/static; every reached source/column lease and current column value are live, including untouched dependencies. | A lease-generation guard plus contiguous row load may replace per-slot object walks if generation changes on every promotion, detach, row retirement and alias change. Recording: distinct rows, used slots and gather visits/timing; proof of exact invalidation and identical values. Retire individual object checks **only** where the generation covers them. The current diagnostic span combines validation and dependency gather, so its timing is not pure check cost. |
| Stage allocation/reset and source mirror `:3384-3440` | Output capacity follows `R × sinks`; scratch is Root-private to VDOM. Mirroring `source.value` is prior-to-projection observable state in generic/fallback paths. | A closed-kernel row lane could avoid mirror writes only after proving no observer of canonical `ScalarSource.value` sees a different state at any callback, exception or fallback boundary; current exported `scalarSource`, `bindSources().read` and generic projectors make this **unknown**, not established. Recording: mirror stores, source reads in actual compiled code, fallback frequency and exceptional traces. Retire the mirror loop only in a proven closed path; a second copy into a new buffer adds work. |
| Kernel and output verification `:3443-3503` | The frozen emitted body is closed syntactically, but runtime association accepts any callable. Output count, indices, sink mask and primitive checks protect public/structural metadata. `seenMask` and output equality preserve first-touch and `Object.is` number semantics. | A genuinely internal compiler-owned kernel could replace staged output arrays and their verify pass with a proven direct output channel, provided all output decisions precede host writes and kernel cannot call user code. Recording: kernel, postkernel stage and output counts; proof of provenance and failure ordering. Retire staging/verification in that closed branch only; retain generic and public entry behavior. |

The host loop is mandatory for changed outputs. | A specialized writer may replace wrapper/equality work if identical host operations, order, exceptions and cache updates are proved. Recording: actual host call count and host/equality interval, plus an identical-output host floor. The 3-per-row host writes are an observed obligation in the measured workload, not removable work. |
| Acknowledgement/cleanup Root `:4863-4886`, VDOM `:3570-3603`, World `:1875-1903`, pending `:143-170` | Exact captured versions gate queue/journal clearing so reentrant newer writes survive; scratch references are cleared even on decline/failure. | A single owner of cut state could replace double journal/queue clearing only with proof that each structure no longer independently carries an obligation. Recording: ack/cleanup counts and time; mutation, disposal and reentrancy tests. Retire old stores/clears together, never skip version checks. |

## Ordering and failure constraints

- Setter actions are computed before flush; a functional updater is user code and may destroy its owner synchronously (`../snapshot/src/owner_state_world.ts:2058-2118`). Dispatch publishes the cell and version, then notifies captured dirty/change listener lists (`:2120-2140`). Any fused path must begin after those effects or reproduce them.
- Root first tries row cut, then lane cut, then generic source cut (`../snapshot/src/component_state_runtime.ts:5081-5155`). A VDOM `null` is a mutation-free preflight decline; Root revalidates every World cell, rebuilds tokens and retries once without recapturing values (`:4933-4975`). A shortcut cannot write hosts before deciding whether fallback is needed.
- VDOM validates packed cells and reached dependencies before mirroring or calling the kernel (`../snapshot/src/vdom_snapshot_runtime.ts:3300-3380`). It mirrors complete captured vectors before any projector/host call (`:3428-3440`). The kernel stages all changed sink values before host application (`:3443-3518`). Generic fallback also projects every affected group before the first host write (`:3520-3565`). Therefore a naive one-pass cell-to-host write changes callback/exception ordering and can expose partial output earlier.
- Root's host mutation wrapper handles publication/reentrancy (`../snapshot/src/component_state_runtime.ts:4540-4568`). Host failure after some writes propagates; Root does not acknowledge and retry the remaining cut because that could repeat prior writes (`:4800-4840`, `:4933-4985`). VDOM updates `lastValue` after a successful host write (`../snapshot/src/vdom_snapshot_runtime.ts:3504-3519`); this partial-commit semantic must survive specialization.
- Promotion, binding refresh/detach, row retirement, keyed changes and disposal invalidate row tokens or leases (`../snapshot/src/owner_state_world.ts:2010-2040`, `:2065-2105`; `../snapshot/src/vdom_snapshot_runtime.ts:2618-2638`, `:3795-3840`, `:4020-4080`, `:4232-4278`). HMR/module replacement is **not proven** to preserve cached program identity in this source review; any future owned-cut cache needs an explicit module/build epoch or must be discarded with the root.

## Unit 2 proof gate

The candidate mechanisms above are conditional replacement paths, not an optimization recommendation. The 128 and 1024 recordings give exact protocol and operation coverage, while the existing phase ledger, overhead controls and residual must be reviewed separately under Unit 1. Before selecting a mechanism, require (1) source/build identity and matched off/on overhead for the same workload, (2) the exclusive span and count for the work to retire, (3) a provenance and escape proof for any skipped check or mirror, (4) a semantic trace for reentrancy, fallback, disposal and partial host failure, and (5) evidence that the old mechanism is removed rather than supplemented. No measured millisecond fraction is inferred from the counts in this report.
